skill.name: golang-security
skill.description: Guides Go security reviews, audits, and secure coding across injection, cryptography, web security, secrets, concurrency, and threat modeling.
skill.summary: Review Go trust boundaries, prioritize vulnerabilities, and plan mitigations with security checklists and STRIDE threat modeling.

security_audit.summary: All 152 static alerts are false positives involving defensive examples, evaluation fixtures, documentation formatting, or unrelated keyword combinations. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection targeting this audit. Two semantic findings identify unsafe XSS guidance and incomplete SSRF defenses that could introduce vulnerabilities into generated applications.

remediation.issue: The XSS quick reference lists text/template as an auto-escaping defense.
remediation.suggestion: Remove text/template from HTML rendering recommendations and explicitly require html/template for untrusted HTML data. Keep the quick reference consistent with the detailed guide.

remediation.issue: The recommended SSRF example omits redirect revalidation and connection-time destination enforcement.
remediation.suggestion: Show an allowlisted HTTP client that validates resolved IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, pins approved destinations during dialing, and rejects or revalidates redirects.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe HTML Template Recommendation
semantic_findings.description: The XSS quick reference lists text/template alongside html/template as an auto-escaping defense. text/template does not escape HTML, so following this recommendation can introduce XSS when rendering untrusted data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The quick-reference row explicitly recommends both packages for auto-escaping. The detailed injection guide correctly uses html/template, confirming a contradictory security recommendation.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete SSRF Mitigation Presented As Safe
semantic_findings.description: The example marked Good checks URL properties but provides no redirect revalidation or connection-time address enforcement. With a normal HTTP client, redirects or DNS changes can bypass preliminary destination checks and reach internal services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recommended snippet contains only preliminary URL checks and an undefined isInternalIP helper. No client transport or redirect policy enforces the destination when a connection occurs.

content.user_title: Review Go Code for Security Risks
content.value_statement: Go services can expose sensitive data through unsafe input handling, weak authentication, and insecure configuration. This skill guides structured reviews, threat modeling, and mitigation planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides review, audit, and coding workflows across injection, cryptography, web security, authentication, and concurrency.
Provides defensive examples for parameterized SQL, scoped filesystem access, secure cookies, TLS, and secrets configuration.
Directs reviewers to trace input origins, validation, call sites, and trust boundaries before reporting findings.
Applies STRIDE threat categories and DREAD scoring to organize threats and remediation priorities.
Documents gosec, govulncheck, race detection, and fuzz testing commands for verification.
Provides checklists for logging privacy, third-party telemetry, authorization, and denial-of-service defenses.
limitations: This is instructional material, not a standalone scanner or a guarantee that generated code is secure.
Examples require independent review; the XSS quick reference is incorrect, and the SSRF example omits essential connection controls.
Executing documented tools requires a compatible Go environment and separately installed dependencies.
Comprehensive dependency management and CI scanner integration are delegated to related skills.

use_cases.title: Review a Go Pull Request
use_cases.description: Trace changed handlers and adjacent data flows to identify exploitable input, authorization, and configuration risks.

use_cases.title: Audit a Service
use_cases.description: Organize a codebase review by vulnerability domain and prioritize findings with evidence and remediation recommendations.

use_cases.title: Model System Threats
use_cases.description: Map trust boundaries across APIs, databases, queues, and external integrations before choosing security controls.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [handler] for security risks. Explain untrusted inputs, existing protections, and recommended fixes. Do not modify files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single HTTP handler.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [pull request or diff] for security issues. Trace relevant call sites and validation. Report evidence, exploitability, severity, and focused remediation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of changed Go code.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure File Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design secure file serving for [service] using Go [version]. Address traversal, symlinks, permissions, resource limits, and regression tests. Explain remaining assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation planning for untrusted file paths.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Trust Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [repository] across injection, cryptography, web security, authorization, and concurrency. Apply STRIDE and DREAD. Separate exploitable findings from hardening recommendations. Propose verification tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced repository audit and threat modeling.

output_examples.input: Review a handler that inserts a request name directly into a SQL query.
output: Finding: SQL injection through a request-controlled name.
Impact: An attacker could change query logic and access unauthorized records.
Recommendation: Pass the name as a query parameter rather than concatenating it.
Verification: Add a regression test with SQL metacharacters and confirm the input remains data.

output_examples.input: Threat-model a webhook receiver that stores events and publishes queue messages.
output: Spoofing and tampering: Verify webhook signatures and enforce a replay policy.
Denial of service: Limit request sizes, processing time, and submission rates.
Information disclosure: Protect transport connections and exclude secrets from logs.
Repudiation: Record event identifiers and processing outcomes in structured audit logs.

best_practices: Provide relevant code, deployment context, Go version, and trust boundaries before requesting a review.
Validate recommendations against current library behavior and distinguish demonstrated exploits from optional hardening.
Verify each mitigation with focused regression tests and appropriate static, race, or fuzz testing.
anti_patterns: Treating instructional snippets or generated fixes as production-ready without independent review.
Sharing live credentials, private keys, or unnecessary personal data in review prompts.
Equating keyword matches or severity scores with proven exploitability.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares compatibility with Codex and Claude Code. It provides instructions and reference documents rather than a separate executable application.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically scan my code?
faq.answer: It guides an assistant through reviews and documents scanner commands. Actual scanning depends on available tools, project access, and user authorization.

faq.question: What Go versions do the examples target?
faq.answer: Filesystem examples prefer os.Root on Go 1.24 or newer. Older-version alternatives are included, with limitations for symlink resistance.

faq.question: Are all recommendations safe to copy directly?
faq.answer: No. The XSS quick reference incorrectly includes text/template, and the SSRF example needs redirect and connection controls. Review examples before use.

faq.question: Can it help prioritize vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes STRIDE threat analysis and DREAD scoring, alongside data-flow tracing and evidence-based review workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace dependency management or CI configuration?
faq.answer: No. It references govulncheck and verification commands, but delegates comprehensive dependency management and CI integration to related skills.
